notes.meaning: Jerusalem is warned to prepare for an enemy attack and a painful siege. Foreign soldiers will surround the city and treat Israel's ruler with great contempt, even striking him across the face with a rod. This deep disgrace showed how low the royal family of David had fallen before God brought rescue.

God promises that a new ruler over his people will be born in the small town of Bethlehem Ephrathah. Even though this village was tiny and counted for little among the clans of Judah, God chose it to be the birthplace of the Messiah. This ruler did not begin his life in Bethlehem, because his life reaches back to eternity as the eternal Son of God.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars hold that the concept of an eternal, pre-existing Messiah does not appear in Jewish literature until later writings like the Similitudes of Enoch.

notes.meaning: God will leave his people under foreign power until the promised child is brought into the world. When that birth takes place, the scattered remnant will return and be united with the rest of God's family. Their long season of suffering will finally give way to the joy of salvation.

differ.view: The woman in labor represents the suffering body of God's people enduring pain before their final deliverance, rather than Mary giving birth.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The woman in labor refers directly to the Virgin Mary giving birth to Christ, which also connects to the woman giving birth in Revelation.

notes.meaning: The coming King will rule and care for his people like a faithful shepherd, using the mighty strength of the Lord. He will lead with divine authority rather than acting like a cruel tyrant. Because his kingdom will reach to the ends of the earth, his flock will rest in lasting security.

This ruler will personally be the peace and safety of his people when dangerous enemies march into the land. Assyria stands for all the worldly powers that attack the people of God. When trouble comes, the Lord will raise up more than enough faithful leaders to protect and guide his flock.

These appointed leaders will push back the enemy and rule over Assyria and Babylon with the sword. The Messiah will use them to rescue his people whenever hostile forces try to cross their borders. Those who plot to destroy God's church will bring ruin upon themselves instead.

The scattered remnant of believers will dwell among the nations like fresh dew and quiet rain on the grass. Just as rain comes straight from God without human effort, this small group will bring spiritual life and blessings purely by God's grace. They will not rely on human strength to accomplish their work.

At the same time, this small remnant will be as brave and strong as a lion among other animals. In God's power, they will stand firm against corrupt nations and spiritual foes who fight against the truth. No hostile power will be able to stop or scatter the flock that God protects.

God promises that his people will lift their hands in total victory over every opponent. All the enemies who plotted against them will be cut off and brought down. The Lord ensures that his faithful followers will outlast and overcome every trial.

The Lord declares that he will take away the war horses and destroy the battle chariots belonging to his people. God strips away these weapons so his followers will stop putting their faith in military hardware. In his kindness, he removes the worldly props that keep them from trusting him alone.

Walled cities and military strongholds will be torn down across the land. In the Messiah's kingdom of peace, heavy defenses will no longer be needed to keep believers safe. God himself will be their high tower and their only wall of protection.

God will wipe out all forms of witchcraft, spells, and fortune-telling from among his people. These wicked practices were forbidden because they turned people away from God toward evil spirits and false claims. The Lord cleanses his church by removing every dark superstition.

All carved statues, molten figures, and sacred pillars will be smashed and cast out. The people will never again bow down and worship objects made with their own hands. God cures their idolatry so that they give their hearts to him alone.

The wooden poles used in the worship of the false goddess Asherah will be completely uprooted. God will also destroy the corrupt towns and pagan centers where this false worship flourished. Nothing that encourages idolatry will be allowed to remain in his presence.

The Lord will execute fiery justice on the nations that refuse to hear and obey his voice. Every ungodly empire that fights against God will face complete destruction. By removing these rebellious enemies, the Lord guarantees lasting peace for his redeemed people.
